## Natural history notes

A large tree squirrel characterized by its bushy tail, variable gray to black or brownish coloration, and often pale underside or facial markings. In Florida, it is found in open pine woodlands, sandhills, oak hammocks, pastures, and other habitats with scattered mature trees. It feeds on acorns, pine seeds, nuts, fruits, fungi, and other plant material, often foraging on the ground and relying on large trees for nesting and cover.
